newsitem.title: SAO TOME AND PRINCIPE: China suspends aid to tiny Sao Tome over Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China suspends aid to tiny Sao Tome over Taiwan.

text.p: China announced on Monday it was halting development projects in impoverished Sao Tome and Principe until the tiny African state made clear whether it intended to establish diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
Accusing Taiwan of waging a campaign of "diplomatic aggression" against the twin island state, a senior Chinese diplomat said all cooperation was being halted temporarily.
Sao Tome President Miguel Trovoada issued a decree last week confirming the establishing of relations with Taiwan, overruling an earlier parliament decision to oppose such a move.

Officials in Sao Tome, one of the world's poorest states, say the African republic has received pledges of aid from Taiwan totalling $30 million over the next decade after deciding to formalise ties with Taipei.
But Beijing has also been an active provider of support, with China currently building the country's first national sports stadium along with residential and engineering projects.
The diplomat, identified only as Mr Wu, told journalists that all the work was being stopped until Sao Tome "took a final decision" on the Taiwan issue.

China regards Taiwan was a rebel province and refuses to maintain full diplomatic relations with countries which recognise the island diplomatically. Taipei has diplomatic ties with some 30 states, most of them small, poor and dependent on its financial largesse.
